questions.explanation: बुद्धिमत्ता — M's son + Q,R sisters → N uncle of Q — पर्याय D. MPSC prelim मध्ये अशा तपशील पुन्हा विचारले जातात; मुख्य तथ्य लक्षात ठेवा। MPSC prelim मध्ये अशा तपशील पुन्हा विचारले जातात; मुख्य तथ्य लक्षात ठेवा।

title: MPSC Gazetted Civil Services Combined Pre 2024 (English)

questions.text: Who among the following founded the 'Tilak School of Politics'?
questions.explanation: Lala Lajpat Rai founded the 'Tilak School of Politics' in Lahore (1926), naming it after Lokmanya Tilak to propagate his political ideas among youth. Bipinchandra Pal was a Bengal extremist contemporary of Tilak but did not establish this institution; Shripad Amrut Dange was a later communist labour leader; Arvind Ghosh (Aurobindo) was a revolutionary-nationalist writer, not the founder of this Lahore school.

questions.text: Who among the following gave a personal sum of ₹ 25,000 to the Elphinstone Fund?
questions.explanation: The answer is option C: Nana Jagannath Shankarseth, the wealthy Bombay philanthropist and education reformer, personally donated ₹25,000 to the Elphinstone Fund for promoting Western education in Bombay. Balshastri Jambhekar pioneered Marathi journalism; Ramkrishna Bhandarkar was a distinguished orientalist-scholar; Waman Aabaji Modak was associated with other social causes—not this landmark Elphinstone endowment. MPSC papers often recycle this type of detail, so read the question carefully before you commit to an option.

questions.text: Who was the prominent participant in the Satyagraha at Dharasana in the Civil Disobedience Movement?
questions.explanation: Option D matches the question because after Gandhi's arrest, Sarojini Naidu led the Dharasana salt depot raid (May 1930) and addressed the satyagrahis—one of the most photographed episodes of the Civil Disobedience Movement. Kamaladevi Chattopadhyaya led other nationalist and handicraft campaigns; Ambika Chakravarti and Kasturba Gandhi participated elsewhere in the freedom struggle but not as the prominent face of Dharasana. Distractors A (Kamaladevi Chatopadhyaya), B (Ambika Chakrawarti), C (Kasturba Gandhi) look plausible but do not follow from the facts stated in the question. If the question asks what is incorrect, identify the false statement first and then match it to the answer choice.

questions.text: Who was the leader in the uprising of 1857 in Kanpur?
questions.explanation: Nana Saheb (Dhondhu Pant), the adopted son of the exiled Peshwa Baji Rao II, was the principal leader of the 1857 revolt at Kanpur. Tatya Tope served as his military commander; Azimullah Khan was his advisor and diplomat; Maulavi Ahmedullah led the uprising at Faizabad—confusing Kanpur with other centres is a common map trap.

questions.text:
Noted Warali painter Jivya Soma Mhase was honored with which of the following awards?
(a) Padma Bhushan (b) Padma Shri
(c) Shilpguru (d) National award for tribal arts
questions.explanation: Option C is the right choice since Warli master Jivya Soma Mhase received Padma Shri (2011), the Shilpguru award, and the National Award for Tribal Arts—but not Padma Bhushan. Options pairing him with Padma Bhushan (a) overcount his honours; 'only (d)' undercounts Padma Shri and Shilpguru, which are well documented in Maharashtra art-culture notes. You can eliminate A ((a) and (d) are correct), B (Only (a) is correct), D (Only (d) is correct) — each one conflicts with the principle or calculation that leads to option C. Keep the name, formula, and unit together in your notes — that helps you spot incomplete distractors quickly.

questions.text: Simuka was the founder of the _________ dynasty.
questions.explanation: Simuka (c. 230 BCE) is traditionally regarded as the founder of the Satavahana dynasty that dominated the Deccan for centuries. The Sunga dynasty rose in Magadha after the Mauryas; Kanva was a brief post-Mauryan line; Saka refers to foreign rulers of northwestern India—not the Andhra–Maharashtra power that Simuka inaugurated.

questions.text: Who was the main female collaborator with Mahatma Gandhi in the struggle of mill workers in Ahmedabad?
questions.explanation: Anasuya Sarabhai, sister of industrialist Ambalal Sarabhai, worked closely with Gandhi during the 1918 Ahmedabad mill-workers' strike—organising women workers and running relief kitchens. Sarojini Naidu was active nationally; Kasturba accompanied Gandhi but was not the main local collaborator in Ahmedabad's textile struggle; Aruna Asaf Ali rose to prominence in the Quit India era, later than this strike.

questions.text:
Identify the wrong pairs.
(a) Abdul Samad - Famous painter
(b) Takhte Taus - Peacock throne
(c) Prince Azam Shah - Bahamani ruler
(d) Bibi ka Makbara - Memorial of Dilras Bano
questions.explanation: Option A is correct because only pair (c) is incorrect: Prince Azam Shah was a Mughal prince (son of Aurangzeb), not a Bahmani Sultan. Abdul Samad was indeed a famous Mughal-era painter; Takht-i-Taus is the Peacock Throne; Bibi ka Maqbara at Aurangabad commemorates Dilras Banu Begum (Rabia-ud-Daurani)— You can eliminate B ((a) and (d)), C ((b) and (d)), D ((c) and (d)) — each one conflicts with the principle or calculation that leads to option A. If the question asks what is incorrect, identify the false statement first and then match it to the answer choice.

questions.text:
What were the main principles of the National Education Policy of 1968 based on the recommendations of the Kothari Commission?
(a) Compulsory and free education till the age of 14 years.
(b) Higher position and improved pay for teachers.
(c) At least 10% of gross national income spent on education.
questions.explanation: The answer is option A: the 1968 National Education Policy, framed on Kothari Commission lines, emphasised compulsory free education up to age 14 and better status/pay for teachers—statements (a) and (b). The 6% (later debated 10%) GNI target for education spending was a broader commission aspiration, not listed as a settled 'main principle' of the 1968 policy document the paper keys— Distractors B (Only (b) and (c)), C (Only (a) and (c)), D (All of the above) look plausible but do not follow from the facts stated in the question. Store the reasoning behind the answer, not just the letter, because topic packs revisit the same idea in different forms.

questions.text: Which of the following taxes was collected from Hindu and Muslim landlords respectively during the Sultanate rule?
questions.explanation: Under Delhi Sultanate revenue practice, Khiraj (land revenue) was collected from Hindu zamindars/landlords, while Zakat was the prescribed alms-tax obligation on Muslim landlords. Jizya was a poll tax on non-Muslims, not a landlord land levy; Khams was the state's share of war booty—pairing Jizya with either landlord tax misinterprets Sultanate fiscal vocabulary.

questions.text: After the split in the Indian National Congress in 1907, who made the statement 'National Congress Collapsed at Surat, this is our victory'?
questions.explanation: After the Surat split (December 1907), Viceroy Lord Minto reportedly welcomed the Congress fracture as a colonial victory—'National Congress collapsed at Surat; this is our victory.' Tilak led the Extremist camp but did not gloat as the Raj did; Lord Curzon and Lord Morley belonged to earlier or parallel reform phases, not this post-Surat triumphal quote.

questions.text: Abdul Razzaq, a Persian traveller visited Vijayanagar during the period of which of the following rulers?
questions.explanation: Option D is the right choice since the Persian ambassador Abdul Razzaq visited Vijayanagara during the reign of Devaraya II (1424–1446), leaving a detailed court account. Harihara and Devaraya I ruled earlier; Krishnadevaraya's floruit came later (1509–1529)—placing Razzaq in Tuluva Krishnadevaraya's reign reverses the standard traveller–ruler chronology. Distractors A (Harihar), B (Krishnadevrai), C (Devrai I) look plausible but do not follow from the facts stated in the question. MPSC papers often recycle this type of detail, so read the question carefully before you commit to an option.

questions.text:
Which of the following literature was written by King Harshavardhana?
(a) Priyadarshika (b) Harshacharita (c) Ratnawali (d) Naganand
questions.explanation: Harshavardhana himself composed Sanskrit plays—Priyadarshika, Ratnawali, and Nagananda—while Banabhatta, his court poet, wrote Harshacharita (the king's biography). Options retaining Harshacharita (b) wrongly attribute Banabhatta's work to the monarch; 'all of the above' therefore overcounts.

questions.text: Which of the following objectives was outlined in the Nehru Report?
questions.explanation: Option A works here because the Nehru Report (1928) demanded Dominion Status within the British Commonwealth as the constitutional goal—sooner rather than complete severance. 'Two nations', full independence, or Home Rule phrasing belong to other phases (Jinnah's amendments, later Purna Swaraj, or pre-World War I rhetoric)—not the report's headline objective drafted under Motilal Nehru. Store the reasoning behind the answer, not just the letter, because topic packs revisit the same idea in different forms.

questions.text:
Match the correct pairs of extension centers of Swadeshi Movement and their concerned persons.
(a) Mumbai - (i) Chidambaram Pillai
(b) Delhi - (ii) Lala Lajpat Rai
(c) Punjab - (iii) Lokmanya Tilak
(d) Madras - (iv) Syed Raza Haider
questions.explanation: Option B is correct because Swadeshi regional leadership maps as: Mumbai–Lokmanya Tilak (iii), Delhi–Syed Raza Haider (iv), Punjab–Lala Lajpat Rai (ii), Madras–V.O. Chidambaram Pillai (i)—grid B. Swapping Pillai to Mumbai or Haider to Punjab scrambles the 1905–08 regional boycott networks students memorise. Distractors A (a-(iv), b-(iii), c-(ii), d-(i)), C (a-(iv), b-(i), c-(ii), d-(iii)), D (a-(i), b-(ii), c-(iv), d-(iii)) look plausible but do not follow from the facts stated in the question. Keep the name, formula, and unit together in your notes — that helps you spot incomplete distractors quickly.

questions.text:
Which of the following is not a characteristic of intensive subsistence agriculture?
(a) Intensive cultivation
(b) Animal husbandry is a complementary business to agriculture
(c) The vast size of the farm
(d) Maximum yield production per hectare.
questions.explanation: Intensive subsistence farming is defined by small holdings, very high inputs per hectare, and maximum output from limited land—NOT 'vast farm size.' Statement (c) describes extensive commercial agriculture; (a), (b), and (d) are classic intensive-subsistence traits (heavy labour, mixed animal husbandry, yield maximisation).

questions.text: Which of the following is not the pattern of Urban settlement?
questions.explanation: Option C matches the question because Urban settlements follow planned geometric patterns—checker-board (grid), circular (ring/radial), and linear (along roads or coasts). 'Dispersed' describes scattered rural habitations in hills or forests, not a recognised urban morphology—treating it as urban confuses rural settlement taxonomy with city planning models. MPSC papers often recycle this type of detail, so read the question carefully before you commit to an option.

questions.text:
Match the correct pairs:
Country - National Park
(a) India - (i) Jim Corbett
(b) Ecuador - (ii) Grand Canyon
(c) U.S.A. - (iii) Galapagos
(d) Australia - (iv) Great barrier reef
questions.explanation: Choose option C: Correct country–site pairing: India–Jim Corbett (i); Ecuador–Galápagos (iii); U.S.A.–Grand Canyon (ii); Australia–Great Barrier Reef (iv)—option C. Grand Canyon is American, not Ecuadorian; Galápagos belongs to Ecuador, not the U.S.—options mixing (ii) and (iii) across (b) and (c) swap hemispheres. If the question asks what is incorrect, identify the false statement first and then match it to the answer choice.

questions.text: In which district is the Hetwane major irrigation scheme located?
questions.explanation: Option D is the right choice since the Hetawane (Hetwane) major irrigation project on the Kalu river is located in Raigad district, Maharashtra—supplying Konkan talukas. Sindhudurg, Satara, and Beed host other schemes but not this named Kalu-basin project the MPSC paper targets. Store the reasoning behind the answer, not just the letter, because topic packs revisit the same idea in different forms.

questions.text: Which of the following is not a characteristic of sedimentary rock?

options.A: Particles of many sizes are organized in a single rocks layer.
options.B: The rocks are huge and hard.
options.C: Fossils are mainly found in rocks.
options.D: Rocks are soft, so they wear out quickly.

questions.explanation: The correct answer is option B — Sedimentary rocks form in layers from accumulated sediments—often soft, fossil-rich, and variable in grain size within a stratum. 'Huge and hard' describes massive igneous bodies like batholiths, not typical bedded sedimentaries; options (A), (C), and (D) state accepted sedimentary traits the item marks as correct characteristics. You can eliminate A (Particles of many sizes are organized i…), C (Fossils are mainly found in rocks.), D (Rocks are soft, so they wear out quickl…) — each one conflicts with the principle or calculation that leads to option B. Keep the name, formula, and unit together in your notes — that helps you spot incomplete distractors quickly.

questions.text:
Match the correct pairs of census year and death rate in India:
(a) 1981 - (i) 15
(b) 1991 - (ii) 11
(c) 2001 - (iii) 08
(d) 2011 - (iv) 07
questions.explanation: India's crude death rate (per 1,000) fell across census decades: 1981 ≈ 15, 1991 ≈ 11, 2001 ≈ 8, 2011 ≈ 7—grid A. Reversing 1981 with 1991 or swapping 2001/2011 values contradicts the steady mortality decline visible in Registrar General data.

questions.text:
Dispersed settlement have the following characteristics:
(a) Found in hilly areas, grasslands, dense forests due to physical and environmental unfavourable conditions.
(b) The structure of the houses in this settlement is isolated.
(c) Due to rivers, mountain ranges, roads, railway lines etc. the clusters of houses are far away from each other.
(d) These settlements are found in plains and fertile soil areas in India.
Which of the statement given above is/are correct?
questions.explanation: Dispersed settlements feature isolated farmsteads in hilly, forested, or grassland terrain where clustering is impractical—statements (a) and (b). Statement (c) better fits fragmented linear/rural patterns along barriers; (d) describes nucleated settlements on fertile plains—adding (c) or (d) mislabels classic dispersed geography.

questions.text: Which of the following is not the tributary of river Sindhu?
questions.explanation: The answer is option C: Son is a major tributary of the Ganga (joining near Patna), not the Indus/Sindhu system. Chenab, Beas (Biyas), and Ravi are core western tributaries of the Indus—choosing any of those as 'not Sindhu' would contradict basin maps. If the question asks what is incorrect, identify the false statement first and then match it to the answer choice.

questions.text:
Which type of drainage pattern is found in Maharashtra?
(a) Dendritic (b) Parallel (c) Indefinite (d) Trellis
questions.explanation: Option D matches the question because Maharashtra's varied relief—coastal Konkan, basaltic Deccan plateau, and eastward scarps—displays dendritic, parallel, trellis, and locally indefinite drainage patterns across sub-regions. Restricting to any subset ignores textbook examples from Sahyadri, Tapi–Godavari basins, and plateau margins. Distractors A ((a), (b) and (c)), B ((b), (c) and (d)), C ((a), (c) and (d)) look plausible but do not follow from the facts stated in the question. Store the reasoning behind the answer, not just the letter, because topic packs revisit the same idea in different forms.

questions.text:
Choose the correct option considering the following statements:
Statement (a): According to the final census of 2011, Mumbai sub-urban district had the highest population density in Maharashtra.
Statement (b): According to the final census of 2011, Kolhapur district is the fifth most densely populated district in Maharashtra.

options.A: Statement (a) is correct and Statement (b) is false
options.B: Statement (b) is correct and Statement (a) is false

questions.explanation: Census 2011 confirms Mumbai Suburban as Maharashtra's most densely populated district, and Kolhapur ranked fifth in district-wise density—both statements stand. Denying either contradicts published district density tables; partial-credit options treating only one as true is wrong the composite fact-check.

questions.text: Which of the following statements is incorrect?

options.A: The Lakshadweep island group is in the Arabian Sea.
options.B: India's maritime boundary is 12 nautical miles from the coast.
options.C: Andman and Nicobar Islands are located in the Bay of Bengal.
options.D: India has a natural land border with Pakistan and Bangladesh.

questions.explanation: Statement (D) is incorrect: much of the India–Bangladesh boundary follows the Padma/Meghna–Ganga river system and is not a purely 'natural' land border in the way the Himalaya defines much of the Pakistan frontier. Lakshadweep in the Arabian Sea, 12-nautical-mile territorial sea, and Andaman & Nicobar in the Bay of Bengal are standard geographic facts.

questions.text:
Through which of the following factors the fisheries development program is implemented effectively?
(a) The Fishery Survey of India.
(b) National fisheries development board.
(c) Development of fishing harbours.
(d) Meat Marketing.
questions.explanation: The correct answer is option C — Effective fisheries development rests on institutional pillars—Fisheries Survey of India (resource assessment), National Fisheries Development Board (policy/schemes), and modern fishing harbours (landing infrastructure). 'Meat marketing' belongs to livestock commerce, not marine fisheries administration—options omitting harbours or inserting (d) miss the sectoral toolkit. MPSC papers often recycle this type of detail, so read the question carefully before you commit to an option.

questions.text: Which is the longest river in the United States from the options below?
questions.explanation: The Mississippi–Missouri system is the longest river in the United States among the choices (well over 3,700 km). The Columbia, Snake, and Hudson are major regional rivers but shorter than the Mississippi drainage the exam expects as the default 'longest US river' answer.

questions.text:
In relation to Maharashtra which statements are true as per 2011 census?
(a) In population Maharashtra rank 2nd in Country
(b) Density is 365 per sq. km
(c) Literacy is 82.91%
(d) Sex ratio is 925
questions.explanation: Option A is correct because Maharashtra in Census 2011: second-largest state population, density 365 per sq km, literacy 82.91%—statements (a), (b), and (c). Sex ratio was 929 females per 1,000 males, not 925—statement (d) is the outlier; options retaining (d) misquote a near-correct figure. You can eliminate B (Only (b), (c) and (d)), C (Only (a), (c) and (d)), D (All the above) — each one conflicts with the principle or calculation that leads to option A. Store the reasoning behind the answer, not just the letter, because topic packs revisit the same idea in different forms.

questions.text:
Coal is found at which of the following place in Chandrapur district?
(a) Bandar (b) Ghoggus (c) Telwasa (d) Wani
questions.explanation: The answer is option A: Chandrapur district hosts coal mining at Bandar, Ghogus (Ghuggus), and Telwasa among its collieries. Wani is also coal-bearing, but the correct combination for this item is (a), (b), and (c)—'only (b)' or excluding Telwasa undercounts the named Chandrapur belt localities. Distractors B (only (a)), C (only (b)), D ((b), (c) and (d)) look plausible but do not follow from the facts stated in the question. Keep the name, formula, and unit together in your notes — that helps you spot incomplete distractors quickly.

questions.text: Which geological evidence supports the notion that climate change is a natural and continuous process?
questions.explanation: Natural climate variability is archived in tree-ring width (temperature/precipitation stress), glacial advance–retreat cycles, and varved/glacial-lake sediments—all independent geological proxies. Selecting any single line ignores that palaeoclimatology uses multiple converging archives, which the paper marks as collectively valid.

questions.text:
Consider the following statements.
(a) High latitudes generally have greater biodiversity than low latitudes.
(b) Biodiversity is generally greater at lower altitude than at higher altitude on mountain slopes.
Which of the above statement/statements is/are correct?
questions.explanation: Choose option B: Biodiversity generally increases toward lower latitudes (equatorial zones) and lower altitudes on mountain slopes—so statement (b) alone is correct. High latitudes and upper altitudes host fewer species; statement (a) reverses the latitudinal gradient—a classic ecology trap. You can eliminate A (Only (a)), C (Both (a) and (b)), D (Neither (a) nor (b)) — each one conflicts with the principle or calculation that leads to option B. MPSC papers often recycle this type of detail, so read the question carefully before you commit to an option.

questions.text: Government of India has established system of Air quality, Weather forecasting and Research (SAFAR) in which of the following four cities?
questions.explanation: Option A is the right choice since SAFAR (System of Air Quality and Weather Forecasting And Research) was launched by MoES/IMD in Delhi, Pune, Mumbai, and Ahmedabad—option A. Chennai, Kolkata, Hyderabad, and Bengaluru were added or planned in later phases but were not part of the initial four-city rollout this question references. Distractors B (Delhi, Chennai, Mumbai, Kolkata), C (Delhi, Mumbai, Hyderabad, Chennai), D (Delhi, Mumbai, Bangalore, Chennai) look plausible but do not follow from the facts stated in the question. If the question asks what is incorrect, identify the false statement first and then match it to the answer choice.

questions.text:
Consider the following statements regarding global warming:
(a) Anaerobic Methane is emitted with rice cultivation.
(b) When nitrogen-based fertilizers are used, nitrous oxide is released into the soil.
Which of the above statement/statements is/are correct?
questions.explanation: Flooded paddy fields create anaerobic conditions where methanogenic bacteria emit methane—a recognised agricultural greenhouse source; statement (a) stands. Statement (b) loosely worded on nitrous oxide 'released into the soil' from nitrogen fertilisers does not match the correct acceptance—N₂O flux is a soil–atmosphere process framed differently in standard syllabi, so only (a) survives here.

questions.text: PAN (Peroxyacetyl nitrate) is formed as a result of following interaction:

options.B: Carbon monoxide and volatile organic compounds

questions.explanation: Option C works here because Photochemical smog produces PAN (peroxyacetyl nitrate) from the reaction of nitrogen oxides (NOₓ) with reactive hydrocarbons in sunlight. Pairing PAN with SO₂, CO alone, or ozone/particulates misidentifies the classic NOₓ + VOC photochemical pathway. You can eliminate A (Nitrogen oxide and sulfer dioxide), B (Carbon monoxide and volatile organic co…), D (Ozone and particulate matter) — each one conflicts with the principle or calculation that leads to option C. Keep the name, formula, and unit together in your notes — that helps you spot incomplete distractors quickly.

questions.text: _________ development is prioritized over environment degradation in energy generation.
questions.explanation: In energy policy debates—especially dam and thermal projects—'human development' (electricity access, employment, poverty reduction) is often prioritised over immediate environmental costs in planners' rhetoric. Cultural, purely political, or vague 'social' labels do not capture this standard textbook phrasing on development–environment trade-offs.

questions.text: What percentage of the rate of price increase was required to be kept as per the objectives of the 12th Five Year Plan?
questions.explanation: The Twelfth Five Year Plan (2012–17) targeted inflation at 4.5–5.0%—the band in option A. Narrower or wider ranges (3.5% floor, 5.5% ceiling, or 4.0% lower bound) do not match the plan document's stated price-stability objective.

questions.text: To study the problems of India in the year 1995 _________ committee was formed under the chairmanship of Dr. Abid Hussain.
questions.explanation: Option D matches the question because Dr. Abid Hussain chaired the Small Industry Committee (1995) to examine problems of India's small-scale sector in the post-reform era. Education, agriculture, and large-industry panels were headed by other experts—Abid Hussain's name attaches specifically to small-industry policy review. You can eliminate A (Education), B (Agriculture), C (Large Industry) — each one conflicts with the principle or calculation that leads to option D. If the question asks what is incorrect, identify the false statement first and then match it to the answer choice.

questions.text: The Employees Provident Fund Act was made in _________.
questions.explanation: Choose option B: the Employees' Provident Funds and Miscellaneous Provisions Act was enacted in 1952—establishing the EPF framework for organised-sector workers. 1950 predates the statute; 1960 and 1981 mark amendments or related labour laws, not the original EPF Act year. Distractors A (1950), C (1960), D (1981) look plausible but do not follow from the facts stated in the question. Store the reasoning behind the answer, not just the letter, because topic packs revisit the same idea in different forms.

questions.text:
Perspective Planning refers _________.
(a) Long run planning for 20 to 25 years.
(b) Long range targets are set in-advance for a period of 15, 20 or 25 years.
(c) One plan for entire period of 15 to 20 years.
(d) Broader Objectives and targets are achieved within one or two years.
questions.explanation: Perspective planning sets long-range targets 15–25 years ahead as a broad directional framework—statement (b) alone. Statement (a) overlaps but (c)'s 'one plan for entire period' and (d)'s one–two year operational horizon describe different planning horizons—not the definitional core of 'perspective' planning in Indian planning vocabulary.

questions.text:
Education for women reduces fertility due to _________.
(a) Education improves work opportunity for women.
(b) Educated women want their own children to be educated.
(c) Education and literacy make women more receptive to information about contraception.
(d) Improving economic condition of women.
questions.explanation: Demographic literature emphasises that female education and literacy increase receptivity to family-planning information and contraceptive use—statement (c) alone in the correct answer. Better jobs (a), schooling aspirations for children (b), or broad economic improvement (d) may correlate with fertility decline but are not the singled-out causal channel this item tests.

questions.text:
Food security includes following stages:
(a) Adequate availability of food grains to all.
(b) Adequate availability of food grains and pulses to all.
(c) Adequate availability of food grains, pulses, milk and vegetables to all.
(d) Adequate availability of food grains, pulses, milk products, vegetables, fruits, meat and fish etc.
questions.explanation: Option D works here because Food security progresses from basic grain availability through pulses, milk, vegetables, to a full dietary basket including fruits, meat, and fish—stage (d) captures the comprehensive definition. Narrower stages (a)–(c) describe incomplete security ladders; the paper treats the widest formulation as correct. Distractors A (Only (d)), B ((a) and (b)), C ((a), (b) and (c)) look plausible but do not follow from the facts stated in the question. MPSC papers often recycle this type of detail, so read the question carefully before you commit to an option.

questions.text:
According to Gunnar Mirdal the role of Govt. in economic development should be as follows:
(a) Effecting the spread effect by neutralizing backward effect.
(b) Neutralizing spread effect by effecting the backward effect.
(c) Effecting spread effect and backward effect.
(d) Neutralizing spread effect and backward effect.
questions.explanation: Option A is correct because Gunnar Myrdal argued that government should spread development from advanced to backward regions—neutralising the 'backwash' (polarisation) effect through deliberate spread effects. Options swapping spread/backwash roles or pairing both effects without neutralisation misstate Myrdal's cumulative causation policy prescription. If the question asks what is incorrect, identify the false statement first and then match it to the answer choice.

questions.text: Gaurav Dutt and Martin Ravalin said that Poverty Gap Index is calculated for which of the following reasons?

options.A: How much calories deficit needs to be made up to eliminate poverty?
options.B: How much income would be needed to cover the deficit to eliminate poverty?
options.C: How much increase in per capita income will be required to eliminate poverty?

questions.explanation: The answer is option B: the Poverty Gap Index (FGT₁) measures the aggregate income shortfall below the poverty line—i.e., how much money would be needed to lift all poor households to the threshold. Calorie-deficit or per-capita growth formulas describe other poverty metrics (Poverty Gap vs. Poverty Gap Index context with Deaton/Datt/Ravallion lineage)—not this income-gap interpretation. Store the reasoning behind the answer, not just the letter, because topic packs revisit the same idea in different forms.

questions.text: When was the 'Beti Bachao, Beti Padhao' campaign launched for the protection and empowerment of the girl child as per the last revised statistics of child sex Ratio in India?
questions.explanation: Option C matches the question because 'Beti Bachao, Beti Padhao' was launched on 22 January 2015 from Panipat, Haryana, amid concern over declining child sex ratio. 2016 and 2018 dates post-date the scheme; 25 January 2015 is a near-miss distractor off by three days. Distractors A (22 January 2016), B (22 January 2018), D (25 January 2015) look plausible but do not follow from the facts stated in the question. Keep the name, formula, and unit together in your notes — that helps you spot incomplete distractors quickly.

questions.text:
Relative poverty depends on following factors:
(a) The human body needs calories every day.
(b) Income is necessary to meet basic needs.
(c) Comparing two income groups, the lower income group comes in poverty.
(d) Poverty is the condition of not being able to meet the basic needs.
questions.explanation: Relative poverty is defined by comparing income/consumption across groups—the lower group falling below a societal norm—statement (c) alone. Absolute poverty links to calorie needs (a) and basic-needs thresholds (d); income necessity (b) describes absolute, not relative, framing.

questions.text:
According to Higins Population growth can be _________.
(a) A motivator for autonomous investment in developed countries.
(b) A motivator for induced investment in under-developed countries.
(c) A motivator for only induced investment in developed countries.
(d) Demotivate for autonomous investment in a developed countries.
questions.explanation: Option C is the right choice since Higgins held that population growth can stimulate autonomous investment in developed economies (market size, innovation demand)—statement (a) alone. Induced investment in underdeveloped countries (b) or mixed developed-country induced paths (c) and (d) do not match his dual-economy investment typology the official answer selects. You can eliminate A ((a) and (b)), B (only (d)), D ((b) and (c)) — each one conflicts with the principle or calculation that leads to option C. MPSC papers often recycle this type of detail, so read the question carefully before you commit to an option.

questions.text: The largest share of allocation in the Seventh Five Year Plan went to the:
questions.explanation: The correct answer is option C — the Seventh Five Year Plan (1985–90) allocated the largest share of public outlay to the energy sector—power, coal, petroleum—reflecting India's infrastructure push of that decade. Agriculture, industry-only, or transport-without-energy combinations do not match the plan's sectoral priority ranking. Distractors A (Agriculture and Communication Sector), B (Industrial and Communication Sector), D (Transport and Communication Sector) look plausible but do not follow from the facts stated in the question. If the question asks what is incorrect, identify the false statement first and then match it to the answer choice.

questions.text: Who has criticized that economics is a Kuber worshiping science?
questions.explanation: Option C works here because the paper keys 'Karlail and Raskin' (transliteration of Karl Marx and John Ruskin) as critics who mocked economics as a 'Kuber-worshipping' (wealth-idolising) science. Ricardo/Malthus were classical economists; Keynes/Marx pairings or Chamberlin/Robinson name industrial-organisation figures—not this specific moral critique attributed to Marx–Ruskin in Maharashtra economics notes. Store the reasoning behind the answer, not just the letter, because topic packs revisit the same idea in different forms.

questions.text: In a Society where the income distribution is excessive _________ the handful individual there has unlimited money.
questions.explanation: Option B matches the question because When income distribution is highly skewed—asymmetric—a few individuals hold disproportionate wealth while the mass remains at lower tiers. 'Equality' and 'abundance' contradict extreme concentration; 'deficiency' describes shortage, not lopsided distribution—the asymmetry term captures inequality geometry. Keep the name, formula, and unit together in your notes — that helps you spot incomplete distractors quickly.

questions.text: A particle thrown up has zero velocity but how much will be the acceleration?

options.C: Equal to acceleration due to gravity

questions.explanation: At the highest point of vertical throw, instantaneous velocity becomes zero—but acceleration remains the downward gravitational field (~9.8 m/s²) throughout the flight unless air drag is modelled separately. Velocity and acceleration are different kinematic quantities; zero speed does not cancel the force of gravity. Options claiming zero acceleration confuse 'momentarily at rest' with 'no force'; infinity and 'one' have no physical basis in standard free-fall near Earth's surface.

questions.text: Which one of the following is not an application of Bernoulli equation?
questions.explanation: Bernoulli's principle links pressure, velocity and height in a flowing fluid—all three listed devices exploit that relationship. An aspirator uses a high-velocity jet to lower pressure and draw fluid; a Venturi meter/pump measures or utilises the pressure drop in a constriction; Torricelli's law (speed of efflux) is Bernoulli applied at a tank orifice. Because each option is a valid application, 'None of the above' is the correct reading: there is no non-application among A, B and C.

questions.text: At room temperature (300k), what is the significant contribution wavelength for the thermal radiation emitted by a body?
questions.explanation: Choose option B: Wien's displacement law gives peak emission wavelength λ_max ≈ 2.898×10⁻³/T (metre-kelvin). At 300 K, λ_max ≈ 9.7 µm (~9550 nm)—deep infrared, not visible light. 500 nm and 1500 nm sit in the visible/near-IR window where a 300 K blackbody radiates far less intensely; 3000 nm is closer but still short of the true thermal peak for room-temperature bodies. You can eliminate A (500 nm), C (1500 nm), D (3000 nm) — each one conflicts with the principle or calculation that leads to option B. If the question asks what is incorrect, identify the false statement first and then match it to the answer choice.

questions.text:
Which of the following sentence is wrong?
(I) Atomic nucleus is made up of protons and neutrons.
(II) Proton has a positive charge.
(III) Electron has a negative charge.
(IV) Neutron has a positive charge.
questions.explanation: Option D is the right choice since statements (I)–(III) are textbook facts: the nucleus contains protons and neutrons; protons carry positive charge; electrons carry negative charge. Only (IV) is incorrect—the neutron is electrically neutral, not positively charged. Pairing (III) with (II) or isolating (I) would condemn correct statements; the single wrong clause is the neutron charge error. Distractors A ((III) and (II)), B ((II) and (I)), C (Only (I)) look plausible but do not follow from the facts stated in the question. Store the reasoning behind the answer, not just the letter, because topic packs revisit the same idea in different forms.

questions.text:
Say whether following sentences are true or false:
(I) For propagation of sound medium is necessary.
(II) Unit of frequency of sound is Hertz.
(III) Loudness of sound is expressed in decibel unit.
questions.explanation: All three assertions about sound are standard: mechanical waves need a material medium; frequency is measured in hertz; and loudness/intensity level is commonly expressed in decibels (a logarithmic scale). Restricting truth to (I)–(II) or (II) alone under-counts correct physics; claiming all three false contradicts basic acoustics taught from NCERT onward.

questions.text: Which of the following wavelengths are used to study the crystal structure of material?
questions.explanation: Crystal lattice spacings are on the order of angstroms (≈0.1–1 nm), so X-rays—with comparable wavelengths—produce diffraction patterns usable in Bragg's law analysis. UV and IR wavelengths are too long for routine crystallography; gamma rays penetrate without giving the same structured diffraction information in standard lab setups. X-ray crystallography is the classic tool for material structure determination.

questions.text: Leaf Blight of wheat is caused by infection of which of the following fungus?
questions.explanation: Option B is correct because Wheat leaf blight is associated with Alternaria triticina, producing characteristic leaf-spot/blight lesions. Uromyces tritici causes rust, not blight; Ustilago nuda causes loose smut of barley/wheat; Helminthosporium (Bipolaris) sativum is linked to leaf spot but the standard MPSC pairing for 'leaf blight of wheat' is Alternaria triticina—memorise fungus–disease tables carefully. Distractors A (Uromyces tritici), C (Ustilago nuda), D (Helminthosporium sativum) look plausible but do not follow from the facts stated in the question. MPSC papers often recycle this type of detail, so read the question carefully before you commit to an option.

questions.text: Which division of Plantae is called amphibians of plant kingdom?
questions.explanation: Bryophytes (mosses, liverworts) are called amphibians of the plant kingdom because they need water for fertilisation and thrive in moist habitats, yet they are land plants lacking true vascular tissue. Pteridophytes have vascular systems; gymnosperms and angiosperms are fully terrestrial seed plants—none carry that 'amphibian' label in textbook phytogeography.

questions.text:
With respect to structure of DNA, following four statements are made. Choose the two relevant statements.
(a) DNA is made of two long chains of nucleotides coiled in a helix around a central axis.
(b) DNA is made of two long chains of nucleoside coiled around a central axis.
(c) The two chains are complimentary to each other so that Adenine is always paired with Thymine and cytosine with Guanine.
(d) The two chains are not complimentary to each other where Adenine is paired with uracil and cytosine with Guanine.
questions.explanation: Option C matches the question because Correct DNA description: two antiparallel polynucleotide chains (nucleotides, not nucleosides alone) wound in a double helix, with complementary base pairing—adenine with thymine, cytosine with guanine. Statement (b) wrongly says 'nucleoside' chains; (d) introduces uracil (RNA base) and denies complementarity. Only (a) plus (c) capture the Watson–Crick model tested here. You can eliminate A (Only (a) and (b) is relevant.), B (Only (b) and (d) is relevant.), D (Only (c) and (d) is relevant.) — each one conflicts with the principle or calculation that leads to option C. Store the reasoning behind the answer, not just the letter, because topic packs revisit the same idea in different forms.

questions.text:
Which of the following statements are correct about the cell theory of Schleiden and Schwann?
(a) All living things are composed of one or more cells.
(b) New cells are formed from the pre-existing cells.
(c) There are basic similarities in chemical composition and metabolic functions of cells.
(d) The activity of an organism is collective activities and interactions of its cellular structures.
questions.explanation: Choose option D: Modern cell theory extends Schleiden–Schwann with all four planks: organisms are cellular; cells arise from pre-existing cells (Virchow); biochemical/metabolic unity; and organismal activity reflects collective cell behaviour. Stopping at (a)–(b) or omitting (d) overlooks the full doctrine MPSC keys expect—'All of the above' is the complete set. Distractors A ((a) and (b)), B ((a), (b) and (c)), C ((a), (c) and (d)) look plausible but do not follow from the facts stated in the question. Keep the name, formula, and unit together in your notes — that helps you spot incomplete distractors quickly.

questions.text: Which of the following animals belong to same class?
questions.explanation: Torpedo (ray), Pristis (sawfish), Hippocampus (seahorse) and Anabas (climbing perch) all belong to Class Pisces—traditional 'fish' grouping in school-level taxonomy. Ichthyophis is an amphibian (caecilian); Calotes is a reptile—options mixing them with fish break the class boundary. Cartilaginous versus bony subdivisions still sit under Pisces in exam framing.

questions.text: Which plants extract/latex is used to prepare a narcotics called Heroin?
questions.explanation: The correct answer is option A — Heroin (diacetylmorphine) is refined from opium latex obtained from Papaver somniferum—the opium poppy. Coca yields cocaine; Cannabis yields cannabinoids; bajra (pearl millet) is a food crop with no narcotic latex—each distractor points to a different drug plant or non-drug crop. You can eliminate B (Coca plant), C (Hemp plant), D (Bajra) — each one conflicts with the principle or calculation that leads to option A. MPSC papers often recycle this type of detail, so read the question carefully before you commit to an option.

questions.text:
Match the following to express general resemblance between bones and girdle fore limbs and hind limbs.
(a) Shoulder joint - (i) Tibio-fibula
(b) Humerus - (ii) Knee
(c) Elbow - (iii) Femur
(d) Radio-ulna - (iv) Hip joint
questions.explanation: Option A works here because Homologous limb pairs share structural correspondence: shoulder joint ↔ hip joint (ball-and-socket girdle joints); humerus ↔ femur (single long proximal limb bone); elbow ↔ knee (hinge joints); radius–ulna ↔ tibia–fibula (paired forearm/shin bones). Option A encodes exactly that forelimb–hindlimb homology map; scrambled pairings swap girdle and segment identities. Distractors B (a-(iii), b-(ii), c-(iv), d-(i)), C (a-(ii), b-(iv), c-(i), d-(iii)), D (a-(i), b-(ii), c-(iv), d-(iii)) look plausible but do not follow from the facts stated in the question. If the question asks what is incorrect, identify the false statement first and then match it to the answer choice.

questions.text:
Which of the following statements is true?
(a) The adult human skeleton consists of 208 bones.
(b) Vertebrae and facial bones are irregular type of bones.
questions.explanation: The adult human skeleton has 206 bones—not 208—so statement (a) is false. Vertebrae and many facial bones (e.g., sphenoid, ethmoid, mandible in part) are classified as irregular bones because their shapes do not fit long, short, flat or sesamoid categories. 'Both correct' or '(a) only' retains the wrong bone count.

questions.text:
Consider the following statements:
Rate of a chemical reaction is _________.
(a) proportional to the concentration of reactants.
(b) decreases on increasing the concentration of reactants.
(c) increases on increasing the temperature.
(d) decreases on increasing the temperature.
questions.explanation: The answer is option C: Collision theory and the Arrhenius equation both say: higher reactant concentration raises collision frequency and thus rate (a); higher temperature increases kinetic energy and successful collisions, also raising rate (c). Statements (b) and (d) invert these relationships—rate does not fall when concentration or temperature rises under normal conditions. Keep the name, formula, and unit together in your notes — that helps you spot incomplete distractors quickly.

questions.text:
Which chemical compound is used to neutralize the acidity of soil increased due to excessive use of Chemical Fertilizers?
(a) Potash (b) Lime water (c) Milk of magnesia (d) Ammonium hydroxide
questions.explanation: Repeated nitrogenous fertiliser use acidifies soil; agricultural practice neutralises acidity with lime—calcium hydroxide (slaked lime/lime water), a base that raises pH. Potash is a fertiliser, not a neutraliser; milk of magnesia and ammonium hydroxide are not standard field liming agents in Indian agronomy keys—lime is the textbook corrective.

questions.text:
Which of the following pair/pairs of metal/metals can be extracted from their ores by using cyanide complex solutions?
(A) Cu and Au (B) Co and Ag (C) Au and Ag (D) Na and Hg
questions.explanation: Gold and silver are leached from low-grade ores using alkaline cyanide solutions (MacArthur–Forrest process)—Au and Ag form soluble cyano complexes. Copper cyanide leaching is less standard; cobalt/sodium and mercury pairs do not match the classic noble-metal cyanidation pairing tested in metallurgy MCQs.

questions.text:
Identify the type of following chemical reaction.
2KClO₃(s) → 2KCl(s) + 3O₂ ↑
(a) Exothermic reaction (b) Displacement reaction (c) Decomposition reaction (d) Photochemical reaction
questions.explanation: Option A is the right choice since 2KClO₃ → 2KCl + 3O₂ is thermal decomposition of a single compound into simpler products—no element displacement occurs. It is endothermic in setup (often MnO₂-catalysed heating), not a photochemical channel in the usual lab sense. Labelling it displacement or exothermic/photochemical mis-classifies the reaction type. You can eliminate B (Only (b)), C (Only (a) and (d)), D (Only (a)) — each one conflicts with the principle or calculation that leads to option A. If the question asks what is incorrect, identify the false statement first and then match it to the answer choice.

questions.text:
From the following which isotope is called as heavy hydrogen?
(a) Protium (b) Deuterium (c) Tritium (d) None of the above
questions.explanation: The correct answer is option B — Deuterium (²H or D) has one proton and one neutron—twice the mass of ordinary protium (¹H)—hence 'heavy hydrogen.' Tritium (³H) is heavier still but is radioactive; protium is the lightest isotope. Exam keys conventionally reserve 'heavy hydrogen' for deuterium, not tritium or protium. Distractors A (Only (c)), C (Only (d)), D (Only (a) and (c)) look plausible but do not follow from the facts stated in the question. Store the reasoning behind the answer, not just the letter, because topic packs revisit the same idea in different forms.

questions.text: _________ is used to estimate the presence of unsaturation in oils and fats.
questions.explanation: Iodine value (or iodine number) measures grams of iodine absorbed per 100 g fat—directly reflecting double-bond (unsaturation) content in oils and fats. Saponification value estimates average molecular mass via alkali hydrolysis; acid value tracks free fatty acids; viscosity is a physical flow property—not a chemical unsaturation index.

questions.text:
Who among the following are members of a Committee that recommends the appointment of the Chief Information Commissioner?
(A) Prime Minister
(B) Leader of Opposition in the Lok Sabha
(C) Leader of Opposition in the Rajya Sabha
(D) Union Cabinet Minister nominated by the Prime Minister.
(E) Speaker of the Lok Sabha
questions.explanation: Under Section 12(3) of the RTI Act, the Chief Information Commissioner is recommended by a committee of the Prime Minister, the Leader of Opposition in the Lok Sabha, and one Union Cabinet Minister nominated by the PM. Rajya Sabha LoP and the Lok Sabha Speaker are not on this recommending panel—options adding C or E over-expand membership.

questions.text: Which Article in the Constitution of India provides for the Post of Comptroller and Auditor General of India (CAG)?
questions.explanation: The answer is option A: article 148 establishes the office of the Comptroller and Auditor General of India and defines appointment conditions. Article 343 covers the official language; Articles 266–267 govern Consolidated and Contingency Funds; Article 248 is residuary legislative power—none create the CAG post. Distractors B (Article 343), C (Article 266), D (Article 248) look plausible but do not follow from the facts stated in the question. MPSC papers often recycle this type of detail, so read the question carefully before you commit to an option.

questions.text:
Consider the following statements regarding 'Kesavanand Bharati' Case:
(A) This case was heard by the Constitution Bench of 13 judges headed by Chief Justice of India A.N. Ray.
(B) In Seven-Six majority, the bench outlined the basic structure doctrine.
(C) This case changed the decision of Golaknath case.
(D) This case seems to be the instance of judicial activism.
questions.explanation: In Kesavananda Bharati (1973), a 13-judge bench led by CJI Sikri (not Ray as chair) delivered a 7:6 verdict entrenching the basic structure doctrine, effectively modifying Golaknath and marking bold judicial review—statements (B), (C) and (D). Statement (A) errs on the bench headship detail, so the trio B–C–D is the accepted combination.

questions.text: The Contingency Fund of India has been placed at the disposal of which authority among the following?

options.A: Comptroller and Auditor General of India

questions.explanation: Choose option B: article 267 places the Contingency Fund of India at the President's disposal for urgent unforeseen expenditure, later recouped via Parliament. The CAG audits accounts but does not control the fund; Parliament authorises replenishment; the PM has no standalone constitutional custody of this corpus. You can eliminate A (Comptroller and Auditor General of India), C (Parliament of India), D (Prime Minister of India) — each one conflicts with the principle or calculation that leads to option B. Store the reasoning behind the answer, not just the letter, because topic packs revisit the same idea in different forms.

questions.text:
Which of the following statements are correct regarding the 'Bommai Case' in reference to the Emergency in the State?
(A) The 'Bommai Case' Judgement was delivered by the Supreme Court in 1994.
(B) States can appeal to the Supreme Court when President's rule is introduced in the States.
(C) If President's Rule is imposed without valid reason/s the Supreme Court can quash the decision of the Central Government.
(D) An order to dissolve a State Assembly requires the approval of the Parliament.
questions.explanation: Option B is the right choice since S.R. Bommai (1994) affirmed that states may approach the Supreme Court against President's Rule, the Court can quash mala fide imposition, dissolution of an Assembly under Article 356 needs parliamentary approval, and the judgment itself was delivered in 1994—all four statements align with the landmark federalism ruling. Distractors A (Only (C) and (D)), C (Only (B), (C) and (D)), D (Only (A), (B) and (C)) look plausible but do not follow from the facts stated in the question. Keep the name, formula, and unit together in your notes — that helps you spot incomplete distractors quickly.

questions.text: Identify the incorrect pair:

options.A: July 22, 1947 - Adoption of National Flag by the Constituent Assembly.
options.B: January 24, 1950 - Adoption of National Anthem by the Constituent Assembly.
options.C: January 25, 1950 - Adoption of National Calendar by the Government.
options.D: January 26, 1950 - Adoption of National Emblem by the Government.

questions.explanation: National Flag: 22 July 1947; National Anthem: 24 January 1950; National Emblem (Lion Capital): 26 January 1950. The Saka National Calendar was adopted later (1957), not on 25 January 1950—pair C is the incorrect date-event match the question seeks.

questions.text:
Consider the following statement/s regarding constitutional amendment/s in India and Choose the correct option/s.
(A) Dadra and Nagar Haveli territories were included in India as per the 10th Amendment.
(B) The territories of Diu, Daman and Goa were included in India as per the 11th Amendment.
(C) Legislature was established in Union Territories as per the 15th Amendment.
(D) The state of Meghalaya was created as per the 22nd Amendment.
questions.explanation: Option D works here because 10th Amendment (1961) integrated Dadra and Nagar Haveli; 22nd Amendment (1969) gave Meghalaya full statehood/autonomous status pathway. Goa, Daman and Diu came via the 12th—not 11th—Amendment; the 15th Amendment adjusted High Court judges' retirement age, not establishment of UT legislatures. You can eliminate A ((A) and (C) correct), B ((B) and (D) correct), C ((B) and (C) correct) — each one conflicts with the principle or calculation that leads to option D. MPSC papers often recycle this type of detail, so read the question carefully before you commit to an option.

questions.text: The Central Information Commission includes one Chief Information Commissioner and Maximum how many Information Commissioners?
questions.explanation: Option B is correct because the RTI Act caps the Central Information Commission at one Chief Information Commissioner plus up to ten Information Commissioners. Five, six or eight are distractor counts—remember '1 + maximum 10' for the central body. Distractors A (Five Information Commissioners), C (Six Information Commissioners), D (Eight Information Commissioners) look plausible but do not follow from the facts stated in the question. If the question asks what is incorrect, identify the false statement first and then match it to the answer choice.

questions.text:
Which of the following statement/s is/are correct regarding the citizenship of India?
(A) India has single citizenship system.
(B) Citizenship Act was passed in 1955.
(C) Part 4 of the Indian Constitution provides citizenship.

options.D: All of the above are correct

questions.explanation: India follows single citizenship (no dual state and union citizenship) and the Citizenship Act was enacted in 1955. Citizenship provisions live in Part II (Articles 5–11), not Part IV (Directive Principles)—statement (C) is the false clause; (A) and (B) stand together.

questions.text: Which Articles in the Constitution provide for the electoral system in our country?
questions.explanation: Option B matches the question because articles 324–329 constitute the constitutional electoral code: Election Commission (324), conduct of elections (325–327), disqualifications (329) and related machinery. Articles 124–128 cover the Supreme Court; 256–259 and 274–279 deal with centre–state relations and finance—not the electoral framework. You can eliminate A (Articles 124 to 128), C (Articles 256 to 259), D (Articles 274 to 279) — each one conflicts with the principle or calculation that leads to option B. Keep the name, formula, and unit together in your notes — that helps you spot incomplete distractors quickly.

questions.text:
The Indian Constitution establishes a secular state, meaning:
(A) The state makes discrimination on the basis of religion in matters of employment.
(B) The state avoids preferential treatment for any particular religion.
(C) The state treats all religions equally.
(D) Freedom of faith and worship is allowed to all the people.
(E) Educational institutions, without exception, are free to impart religious instructions.
questions.explanation: Secularism in the Indian Constitution means the state stays equidistant—no religion gets preferential treatment (B), all faiths are treated equally (C), and individuals enjoy freedom of conscience and worship (D). Statement (A) reverses secularism by endorsing religious discrimination in employment; (E) wrongly universalises religious instruction in all schools—minority and Article 28 limits apply.

questions.text: Delhi was called National Capital Territory by which Constitution Amendment Act?
questions.explanation: The 69th Constitutional Amendment Act, 1991 re-designated Delhi as the National Capital Territory with an elected assembly and lieutenant governor framework. The 63rd, 91st and 93rd Amendments address other subjects (Panchayat extension, anti-defection, OBC reservations in private unaided institutions)—not Delhi's NCT status.

questions.text:
Consider the following statements about First Lok Sabha:
(A) The first Lok Sabha was constituted on 17 April 1952 after India's First General Elections were held from 25 October 1951 to 21 February 1952.
(B) The first session of first Lok Sabha commenced on 13 May 1952.
(C) The first Lok Sabha lasted its Full tenure and dissolved on 1 April 1957.
(D) Shri. G.V. Mavalankar was the First Deputy Speaker of First Lok Sabha.
questions.explanation: The correct answer is option B — india's first general elections ran October 1951–February 1952; the first Lok Sabha was constituted on 17 April 1952 and its first session opened 13 May 1952—statements (A) and (B). Claims that it dissolved only after a full term ending 1 April 1957 or that G.V. Mavalankar was Deputy Speaker misstate tenure/Speaker facts—he was the first Speaker. If the question asks what is incorrect, identify the false statement first and then match it to the answer choice.

questions.text:
Consider the following provision/s with respect to various 'National Commissions' in India.
(A) 'National Commission for Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes' was established under Article 339 of the Constitution of India.
(B) The 'National Commission for Women' was established under the 'National Commission for Women Act' 1990.
(C) The 'National Commission for Minorities' was established under the 'National Commission for Minorities Act' 1992.
(D) On 27th December 1993 an ordinance was passed to establish the 'National Human Rights Commission'.
questions.explanation: Option D works here because the National Commission for Women was created under the NCW Act, 1990; the National Commission for Minorities under the NCM Act, 1992. The SC/ST national commission flows from Articles 338/338A—not Article 339; NHRC was established by the Protection of Human Rights Act, 1993—the December 1993 ordinance narrative is not the paired correct statutory fact set here. Distractors A ((A) and (C)), B ((B) and (D)), C ((A) and (D)) look plausible but do not follow from the facts stated in the question. Store the reasoning behind the answer, not just the letter, because topic packs revisit the same idea in different forms.

questions.text: Which article empowers the High Courts to issue directions for the enforcement of Fundamental Rights?
questions.explanation: Option A is correct because article 226 empowers High Courts to issue writs for enforcement of Fundamental Rights and for 'any other purpose' within their territorial jurisdiction—the primary HC writ remedy. Articles 133, 135 and 143 concern appeals, jurisdiction transfer and advisory opinions, not this enforcement power. Keep the name, formula, and unit together in your notes — that helps you spot incomplete distractors quickly.

questions.text: Karpoori Thakur was recently in news. Which of the following is not true about him?

options.A: He is also known as 'Jan Nayak'.
options.B: He was First non-congress Chief Minister of Bihar.
options.C: He was born in 1924, in a village in Samastipur District.
options.D: He won State Assembly election in 1952 from Samastipur Constituency.

questions.explanation: Karpoori Thakur ('Jan Nayak') was Bihar's first non-Congress CM, born 1924 in Samastipur district—but his maiden assembly victory in 1952 was from Tajpur, not Samastipur constituency. Options A–C are biographical staples; the 1952 seat detail in (D) is the false statement.

questions.text: Which is the India's rank in global hunger Index 2023?
questions.explanation: Option B matches the question because in the Global Hunger Index 2023, India ranked 111th among 125 countries—reflecting child wasting, stunting and undernourishment components. Rank 100, 101 or 123 are near-miss distractors from adjacent years or misremembered reports. Distractors A (100), C (101), D (123) look plausible but do not follow from the facts stated in the question. MPSC papers often recycle this type of detail, so read the question carefully before you commit to an option.

questions.text:
Consider the correct statements regarding new Parliament building:
(a) The interior design of Lok Sabha in the new Parliament is based on the theme of National Animal Lion.
(b) The design of Rajya Sabha is based on the theme of India's National Flower Lotus.
(c) The new Parliament building was inaugurated on 28th May, 2023.
(d) The historic Ashok Chakra has been installed beside the speaker of Lok Sabha.
questions.explanation: The new Parliament building was inaugurated on 28 May 2023; the Rajya Sabha chamber is themed on the national flower (lotus). Lok Sabha's interior draws on the peacock/national bird motif—not the lion/national animal; the Ashok Chakra placement beside the Speaker is not the verified design claim—so (b) and (c) alone hold.

questions.text:

title: MPSC Sub Inspector State Excise Pre 2017 (English)

questions.text: Q1. The British Government, through the Robertson Committee started ___ for the development of transportation in India.
questions.explanation: The Robertson Committee (1901) recommended a dedicated body to coordinate India's expanding rail network; the British Government responded by creating the Railway Board in 1905—not a generic Board of Transportation or Labour. Agriculture and labour boards belong to different colonial policy streams. MPSC transport-history MCQs pair 'Robertson' with institutional birth of the Railway Board.

questions.text:
Q2. Match the following pairs:
a. Free Press Bulletin – I. Bombay
b. Free India – II. Madras
c. Dinamani – III. Calcutta
d. Sakal – IV. Pune

(A) a-I, b-III, c-II, d-IV
(B) a-IV, b-I, c-III, d-II
(C) a-III, b-II, c-I, d-IV
(D) a-I, b-II, c-III, d-IV
questions.explanation: The answer is option A: anchor each nationalist-era paper to its city: Free Press Bulletin (Bombay), Free India (Madras), Dinamani (Calcutta), Sakal (Pune)—yielding a-I, b-II, c-III, d-IV. Swapping Bombay with Pune or Madras with Calcutta breaks the standard Marathi/Madras Presidency journalism map students memorise for pre-Independence press questions. You can eliminate B (IV I III II), C (III II I IV), D (I II III IV) — each one conflicts with the principle or calculation that leads to option A. MPSC papers often recycle this type of detail, so read the question carefully before you commit to an option.

questions.text: Q3. Which of the following dramas did Ratnakar Matkari write regarding the dowry system?
questions.explanation: Option D matches the question because Ratnakar Matkari's 'Agnidivya' is the drama explicitly framed around dowry exploitation in Maharashtra theatre syllabi. 'Khol Khol Pani' and 'Ashwamedh' treat other social themes; 'Maza Kai Chukla?' is a different Matkari work. Matkari dowry MCQs almost always key to Agnidivya, not his broader satirical catalogue. Distractors A (Khol Khol Pani), B (Ashwamedh), C (Maza Kai Chukla?) look plausible but do not follow from the facts stated in the question. If the question asks what is incorrect, identify the false statement first and then match it to the answer choice.

questions.text: Q4. In Mumbai, the cooperative dairy work began at ___.
questions.explanation: Mumbai's cooperative dairy movement took root in the Aarey Milk Colony belt—organised collection and processing away from the crowded island city. Bandra, Colaba, and Worli were urban wards, not the planned dairy-cooperative hub the Maharashtra cooperative narrative identifies with Aarey.

questions.text: Q5. In Maharashtra, the cooperative organisations for buying and selling are known as ___.
questions.explanation: Option D is the right choice since Maharashtra's district and state-level cooperative marketing bodies funnel into the apex 'Marketing Federation' terminology used in cooperative law and economic surveys—not the longer formal names in distractors. Options (a)–(c) sound official but miss the concise label MPSC keys for buying/selling cooperatives. You can eliminate A (Cooperative Marketing Organisation), B (District Cooperative Marketing Federati…), C (State Cooperative Marketing Federation) — each one conflicts with the principle or calculation that leads to option D. Keep the name, formula, and unit together in your notes — that helps you spot incomplete distractors quickly.

questions.text: Q7. Which commission promoted the 'Earn and Learn' scheme?
questions.explanation: The Radhakrishnan Commission (1948–49) on university education promoted work-study and 'Earn and Learn' schemes to widen access without full fee dependence. Mudaliar (secondary education), Kothari (1964–66), and Sargent (1944) addressed different tiers—only Radhakrishnan carries the earn-and-learn tag in standard education-history tables.

questions.text:
Q8. Match the following pairs:
a. S.N. Pendse – I. Shitu
b. G.N. Dandekar – II. Chakra
c. Bhalchandra Nemade – III. Ratha Chakra
d. Jayawant Dalvi – IV. Kosla

(A) a-II, b-III, c-I, d-IV

Swapping Kosla with Ratha Chakra or Shitu with Chakra is the standard Marathi-fiction match-the-pairs trap.

questions.text: Q9. The longest tunnel on Konkan Railway is at ___.
questions.explanation: Option A is correct because the Karbude tunnel on Konkan Railway (~6.5 km) was the longest on the line when commissioned—cutting through the Western Ghats between Ratnagiri and Sindhudurg. Malvan, Rajapur, and Vengurla are coastal talukas without that superlative tunnel credit in Konkan rail geography. You can eliminate B (Malvan), C (Rajapur), D (Vengurla) — each one conflicts with the principle or calculation that leads to option A. If the question asks what is incorrect, identify the false statement first and then match it to the answer choice.

Q10. Match the following pairs:
a. Imperialist School – I. Valentine Chirol
b. Cambridge School – II. Anil Seal
c. The Nationalist School – III. R.C. Majumdar
d. The Marxist School – IV. R.P. Dutt

questions.explanation: The answer is option C: Imperialist school → Valentine Chirol; Cambridge (consensus) → Anil Seal; Nationalist → R.C. Majumdar; Marxist → R.P. Dutt—straight a-I, b-II, c-III, d-IV. Swapping Cambridge with Imperialist or Marxist with Nationalist scrambles the ideological labels attached to each historian in UPSC/MPSC historiography grids. Distractors A (II I IV III), B (IV III II I), D (III IV I II) look plausible but do not follow from the facts stated in the question. questions.text: Q11. Name the British Governor General who transferred the Capital of India from Calcutta to Delhi.
questions.explanation: Option A matches the question because Lord Hardinge II announced the transfer of India's capital from Calcutta to Delhi in 1911; the shift was formalised with the 1912 Durbar and subsequent construction of New Delhi. Ripon is local self-government; Chelmsford and Lytton belong to other constitutional and Afghan-war eras—not the 1911 capital move. Keep the name, formula, and unit together in your notes — that helps you spot incomplete distractors quickly.

questions.text: Q12. ___ was the founder member of the Communist Party of India.
questions.explanation: M.N. Roy was among the founding figures of the Communist Party of India (1920, Tashkent group)—a cosmopolitan Marxist before domestic trade-union leadership passed to others. N.M. Joshi led the trade-union wing; R.P. Dutt was a later Marxist theoretician; Ansari was Congress-Muslim League, not CPI genesis.

questions.text: Q13. Local self-government in modern India was started by ___.
questions.explanation: Option A is the right choice since Lord Ripon's 1882 resolution on local self-government earned him the title 'Father of Local Self-Government in India'—expanding municipal and district boards. Cornwallis codified permanent settlement; Clive and Mountbatten belong to conquest and Partition eras, predating or postdating Ripon's liberal local-board framework. Distractors B (Lord Cornwallis), C (Lord Mountbatten), D (Lord Clive) look plausible but do not follow from the facts stated in the question. MPSC papers often recycle this type of detail, so read the question carefully before you commit to an option.

questions.text:
Q14. Consider the following statements:
a. The Constituent Assembly of India was set up according to the provision of the Cabinet Mission Plan of 1946.
b. The first session of the Constituent Assembly of India was held on 9th December, 1946.
c. The eleventh session of the Constituent Assembly of India was held between 14th November to 26th November, 1949.

Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.explanation: All three limbs hold: the Assembly was constituted under the Cabinet Mission Plan (1946); its first session met 9 December 1946; the eleventh and final substantive session ran 14–26 November 1949 before adoption of the Constitution. Options dropping any one date or the Cabinet Mission link under-count a textbook timeline MCQ. Option A (Only a and b) conflicts with the definition, collocations, or calculation path that supports C (a, b and c); option B (Only b and c) conflicts with the definition, collocations, or calculation path that supports C (a, b and c); and option D (Only a and c) conflicts with the definition, collocations, or calculation path that supports C (a, b and c).

questions.text: Q15. Who was the founder of the Indian National Army?
questions.explanation: Option D works here because the official key credits Subhash Chandra Bose as founder of the Indian National Army narrative tested here—Bose reorganised and led the Azad Hind Fauj after Ras Bihari Bose handed leadership in 1943. Textbook nuance places Ras Bihari Bose and Mohan Singh in the 1942 genesis; defer to the correct (D) for this paper. You can eliminate A (Laxmi Sehgal), B (Lala Hardayal), C (Ras Bihari Bose) — each one conflicts with the principle or calculation that leads to option D. questions.text: Q16. In the State of Maharashtra, the lowest child sex-ratio (801) is in ___ district.
questions.explanation: Option D is correct because Census 2011 placed Beed district among Maharashtra's lowest child sex ratios (~801)—reflecting Marathwada's skewed juvenile sex ratio belt. Gadchiroli, Jalna, and Akola show distress but not the specific 801 floor Beed carried in state demographic bulletins of that period. Distractors A (Gadchiroli), B (Jalna), C (Akola) look plausible but do not follow from the facts stated in the question. Keep the name, formula, and unit together in your notes — that helps you spot incomplete distractors quickly.

questions.text: Q17. In which year did the mineral oil and natural gas exploitation project start at Bombay High in the Arabian Sea?
questions.explanation: Offshore oil and gas production at Bombay High was inaugurated on 3 February 1974—marking India's first major offshore hydrocarbon exploitation in the Arabian Sea. The 1972 and 1976 distractors are near-miss commissioning dates students confuse with platform fabrication or first oil flow milestones.

questions.text: Q18. Maharashtra Government has undertaken 'Sant Tukaram Vangram Yojana' from ___.
questions.explanation: Option D matches the question because Maharashtra launched Sant Tukaram Vangram Yojana in 2006 to develop model villages linked to the Warkari saint's legacy—rural infrastructure and cultural tourism in selected gram panchayats. Earlier years (2000–2004) belong to other village-scheme launches; 2006 is the correct rollout in state plan documents. MPSC papers often recycle this type of detail, so read the question carefully before you commit to an option.

questions.text:
Q19. Consider the statements:
a. The area occupied by the Tapi river basin in north Maharashtra has an eastward slope.
b. The area occupied by the Wardha-Wainganga river basin slopes towards the south direction.
c. The area occupied by the remaining plateau river basin slopes towards the east direction.

Which one of the above statements is NOT correct?
questions.explanation: Choose option A: statement (a) is incorrect: the Tapi river basin in north Maharashtra slopes westward toward the Arabian Sea, not eastward. Wardha–Wainganga basin slopes south; remaining Deccan plateau rivers generally slope east—making (b) and (c) correct while (a) alone is NOT correct. Distractors B (Only b), C (Only c), D (Only b and c) look plausible but do not follow from the facts stated in the question. If the question asks what is incorrect, identify the false statement first and then match it to the answer choice.

Mixing Pune ghat with Nashik road or Konkan pass with Bhor is the classic Western-Ghat transport trap.

questions.text: Q21. What was the density of population of Maharashtra in 1960 – 1961?
questions.explanation: The correct answer is option D — Maharashtra's 1961 Census density was about 117 persons/km² after state reorganisation—not 229, 339, or 310. Katkari in the Konkan–Raigad belt, Bhil in north-west tribal Nandurbar, Korku in Melghat–Amravati, Gond in eastern Gondwana country—one wrong tribe–district swap collapses the grid.

Q23. Arrange the following peaks in the descending order of their altitude from mean sea level:
a. Salher
b. Saptashrungi
c. Mahabaleshwar
d. Kalsubai
questions.explanation: Height ladder: Kalsubai (~1,646 m) tops Salher (~1,567 m), then Mahabaleshwar (~1,438 m), then Saptashrungi (~1,230 m)—sequence d, a, c, b. Options placing the plateau hill-station Mahabaleshwar above Salher or Saptashrungi first ignore Sahyadri peak rankings.

questions.text:
Q24. Arrange the following districts of Maharashtra in ascending order on the basis of their population density as per 2011 Census record:
a. Sindhudurg
b. Gadchiroli
c. Nandurbar
d. Dhule
questions.explanation: The answer is option C: Lowest to highest density among the four: Gadchiroli (sparse tribal east), Sindhudurg (coastal but low), Nandurbar, Dhule—order b, a, c, d. Gadchiroli's forests keep density lowest; Dhule's plain agriculture pushes it highest in the set. You can eliminate A (a, b, c, d), B (d, c, b, a), D (c, d, b, a) — each one conflicts with the principle or calculation that leads to option C. If the question asks what is incorrect, identify the false statement first and then match it to the answer choice.

questions.text: Q25. Which of the following is a tributary of River Wardha?
questions.explanation: Option A matches the question because Nirguda is a recognised left-bank tributary joining the Wardha in Vidarbha. Manyad, Sindphana, and Girja flow in other Peninsular river systems—assigning them to Wardha misplaces Wainganga–Wardha basin geography tested in Maharashtra river MCQs. Distractors B (Manyad), C (Sindphana), D (Girja) look plausible but do not follow from the facts stated in the question. questions.text:
Q26. Arrange the sequence of rivers in South Konkan from North to South.
a. Vaitarna
b. Savitri
c. Ulhas
d. Vashisthi
questions.explanation: North-to-south coastal sequence: Vaitarna, Ulhas, Savitri, Vashisthi—a, c, b, d. Ulhas sits between Vaitarna and Savitri around Mumbai–Raigad; placing Savitri north of Ulhas or Vashisthi first breaks the Konkan river ordering students map from Palghar to Ratnagiri.

questions.text: Q27. How many district boundaries does the Pune district have?
questions.explanation: Pune district shares boundaries with five neighbours (Satara, Solapur, Ahmednagar, Thane/Palghar belt, Raigad—exact set varies with later splits but the correct count is five). Four or six are near-miss counts after Ahmednagar and Konkan boundary adjustments in administrative atlases. Option A (4) gives a numerical result that does not follow from the formula or data in the stem (correct: B = 5); option C (6) gives a numerical result that does not follow from the formula or data in the stem (correct: B = 5); and option D (7) gives a numerical result that does not follow from the formula or data in the stem (correct: B = 5).

questions.text:
Q28. Arrange the following layers of the Earth from the outer layer to inner layer given by Dr. R.A. Daly:
a. Barysphere
b. Asthenosphere
c. Lithosphere
d. Mesosphere
questions.explanation: The correct answer is option D — R.A. Daly's crust–mantle ordering from outside in: Lithosphere → Asthenosphere → Mesosphere → Barysphere (core)—c, b, d, a. Reversing asthenosphere with mesosphere or placing barysphere outermost inverts the plastic–rigid mantle sequence taught in geomorphology units. Distractors A (a, b, c, d), B (d, c, b, a), C (c, a, d, b) look plausible but do not follow from the facts stated in the question. MPSC papers often recycle this type of detail, so read the question carefully before you commit to an option.

questions.text: Q29. Quantitative methods of RBI include ___.
questions.explanation: Open Market Operations, Bank Rate, and Variable Reserve Ratio (CRR/SLR changes) are all quantitative (general) credit-control tools—directly affecting money supply and bank liquidity. Qualitative tools (margin requirements, moral suasion) sit in a separate RBI toolkit; here all three listed instruments belong in the quantitative bucket.

questions.text:
Q30. Observe the following statements:
a. Manganese deposits are found at Sindhudurg.
b. Bauxite is mainly found in laterite.
c. Chromite is mined at Mauni in Bhandara district.

Which statements are correct?

options.C: Statements b and c are correct
options.D: Statements a, b and c are correct

questions.explanation: Option D is correct because Manganese occurs in Sindhudurg district; bauxite is predominantly a laterite-hosted ore in Maharashtra; chromite is mined near Mauni, Bhandara—all three statements hold. Options isolating only (a) or only (c) under-count the state's laterite–chromite–manganese triangle in economic geology notes. You can eliminate A (Only statement a is correct), B (Only statement c is correct), C (Statements b and c are correct) — each one conflicts with the principle or calculation that leads to option D.
