questions.text:
Consider the following statement about ethylene and choose the correct
option.
(a) It is the only aerobic hormone that is useful for fruit development.
(b) The root and ripening fruits of the plant are most abundant in two places of
ethylene.
(c) Decreased amount of carbon dioxide acts as an inhibitor for ethylene.
questions.explanation: Ethylene is a gaseous hormone promoting fruit ripening and senescence; roots and ripening fruits are major ethylene sources (b)—the sole correct correct line. Calling it 'only aerobic hormone' (a) is nonsense; CO₂ usually inhibits ethylene action, not decreased CO₂ (c). Key A isolates (b).

questions.text:
Make the correct pairs of germination.
(a) Hypogeal | i) Occurring under specific conditions
(b) Epigeal | ii) Seed germination underground
(c) Vivipary germination | iii) Seed above ground with germination
questions.explanation: Option D is correct because Hypogeal germination: cotyledons stay below soil—underground seedling stage (ii). Epigeal: cotyledons rise above ground (iii). Vivipary: seeds germinate while still on the parent plant under special conditions (i). Key D: a-ii, b-iii, c-i. You can eliminate A ((ii) (i) (iii)), B ((iii) (ii) (i)), C ((i) (iii) (i)) — each one conflicts with the principle or calculation that leads to option D. questions.text:
Consider the following statements regarding p ollination.
(a) Pollination is the transfer of pollen grains from the anther to the stigma of
the female flower.
(b) When pollination occurs in the same flower or two flowers of the same
type, it is called cross pollination.
(c) When the pollination takes place from one plant flower to another plant
flower it is called self pollination.
Choose the correct statement/s from the above.
questions.explanation: Pollination is pollen transfer from anther to stigma (a)—correct definition. (b) and (c) swap self vs cross pollination labels. Same-flower/same-plant pollen is self-pollination; different plants is cross (xenogamy). Only (a) is reliable; options bundling (b) or (c) inherit the terminology reversal trap.

questions.text: Which among the following are known as precursors of ethylene?
questions.explanation: Ethylene biosynthesis proceeds from methionine via SAM and ACC; amino-acid origin is syllabus-standard (b). Acetic/butyric acid precursors are distractors. Methionine + amino-acid framing is the correct pair.

(b) Nitrification | ii) Conversion of nitrogen-containing compounds into ammonia

questions.explanation: Choose option B: ammonification converts organic nitrogen compounds to ammonia (ii). Nitrification oxidises ammonia → nitrite → nitrate (iii). Denitrification returns nitrate to N₂ gas (i). Key B: a-ii, b-iii, c-i—follow the nitrogen-cycle direction arrows. (a) Abbasic acid is a naturally occurring growth retarding hormone.
(b) It is called stress hormone.
(c) These are formed in older leaves, flowers, fruits.

options.D: All of the above are correct

questions.explanation: Option D is the right choice since aBA is a natural growth inhibitor/stress hormone (a), dubbed stress hormone for drought/frost responses (b), synthesised in mature leaves, flowers, and fruits (c). All three align with inhibitor physiology—key D. Distractors A (Only (a), (b) are correct), B (Only (b), (c) are correct), C (Only (a), (c) are correct) look plausible but do not follow from the facts stated in the question. questions.text:
Observe the following statements regarding Anaerobic respiration.
(a) Oxygen is not required for anaerobic respiration to occur.
(b) anaerobic respiration takes place in cytoplasm itself
(c) anaerobic respiration yields less energy than aerobic respiration.
(d) This activity is observed in germinating seeds as well as in some bacteria.
Choose the correct statements from the above.

options.D: All of the above are correct

questions.explanation: Anaerobic respiration needs no O₂ (a), occurs in cytoplasm (b), yields less ATP than aerobic path (c), and appears in germinating seeds and facultative anaerobes (d). Fermentation in rice seedlings and yeast is textbook—all four stand.

questions.text:
Consider the following statements about cytokinin and select the correct
statement option.
(a) Adequate cytokinin along with auxin helps in organogenesis.
(b) Cytokinin prolongs senescence in plants.
(c) It nullifies apical dominance.

options.D: All of the above are correct

questions.explanation: Cytokinin with auxin induces organogenesis/shoot formation in tissue culture (a). Cytokinin delays senescence (b)—contrasts with ABA/ethylene. It relieves apical dominance when applied to lateral buds (c). All three are classic cytokinin effects.

questions.text:
Match the correct pairs.
(a) Long day plants | i) Coffee, tobacco
(b) Short day plant | ii) Tomato
(c) Day neutral plants | iii) Carrot, beet
(d) Biennial plants | iv) Cabbage, spinach, oat

Distractors B ((a)-(ii), (b)-(iv), (c)-(i), (d)-(iii)), C ((a)-(i), (b)-(iii), (c)-(ii), (d)-(iv)), D ((a)-(iii), (b)-(iv), (c)-(ii), (d)-(i)) look plausible but do not follow from the facts stated in the question. Store the reasoning behind the answer, not just the letter, because topic packs revisit the same idea in different forms.

questions.text:
Which of the following theories concludes that living cells are responsible
for water transfer?
questions.explanation: Root pressure theory ascribes ascent partly to living root cell osmotic pumping—bio-active mechanism (A). Capillary and pure transpiration theories emphasise physical dead-column or evaporative pull without living pump emphasis.

questions.text:
Consider the following statement/s and choose the correct option.
(a) There are approximately seven million species of animals on earth.
(b) The method of animal classification used by Aristotle is called Artificial
classification method.
(c) John Ray, Linnaeus used naturalistic method of classification.

options.D: All of the above are correct

questions.explanation: Animal diversity estimates in Maharashtra board zoology hover around seven million described and projected animal species on Earth—statement (a) is syllabus-safe. Aristotle's early grouping by habitat, movement, and body covering is textbook 'artificial classification'—(b) stands. John Ray and Linnaeus are credited with natural/naturalistic systems based on structural affinity, but this paper keys (c) as incorrect—likely because the syllabus treats Linnaeus's sexual system as artificial and reserves 'natural' for later phylogenetic work. Lock (a)+(b), reject (c).

questions.text:
Consider the following statement about the phylum Porifera and choose
the correct option.
(a) All types of sponges belong to this group.
(b) They have openings on the body called ostiums while larger openings on the
top are called osculums.
(c) Osculum acts like mouth while ostium acts like anus.
questions.explanation: The answer is option C: Every true sponge sits in Porifera—(a) is a clean phylum–group match. Water enters through numerous small incurrent pores (ostia) and leaves through the large excurrent opening (osculum)—(b) is anatomically sound. Statement (c) reverses flow logic: the osculum is the exit ('ex-current'), not the mouth analogue, and ostia are entry pores, not an anal opening. Only (a) and (b) survive. You can eliminate A (Only (a) and (c) are correct), B (Only (b) and (c) are correct), D ((a), (b) and (c) are all correct) — each one conflicts with the principle or calculation that leads to option C. MPSC papers often recycle this type of detail, so read the question carefully before you commit to an option.

questions.text:
Consider the following statement about the group Cilantrata/Cnidaria
and select the correct option.
(a) The body has a single mouth and tentacles around it.
(b) The bodies of animals in this group are radially symmetrical and diploblastic.
(c) Animals in this group live in water as well as on land.

options.D: All of the above are correct

questions.explanation: Option A matches the question because Cnidarians/Coelenterates carry a single gastrovascular opening ringed by tentacles—(a) fits Hydra, jellyfish, and coral polyps. Radial symmetry plus diploblastic body wall (epidermis + gastrodermis with mesoglea) defines the phylum—(b) is core syllabus. They are overwhelmingly aquatic; no marine cnidarian lineage completes life on land—(c) is the dud limb. Pair (a) with (b), drop (c). Distractors B ((b), (c) orrect and (a) incorrect), C ((a), (c) orrect and (b) incorrect), D (All of the above are correct) look plausible but do not follow from the facts stated in the question. If the question asks what is incorrect, identify the false statement first and then match it to the answer choice.

questions.text:
Observe the following statements and choose the option of the correct
statement.
(a) Polychaetes of class Annelida have open blood circulatory system.
(b) Hirudinia animals of class Annelida have closed blood circulatory system.
questions.explanation: Polychaete annelids (Nereis, etc.) actually possess a closed circulatory system with dorsal and ventral vessels—so statement (a) as written is false. Hirudinea (leeches) rely on haemocoelic/open-type circulation without true capillary networks—statement (b) is also false as a 'closed system' claim. both statements are wrong; don't force one to be true.

questions.text:
Match the correct pairs.
(a) Ferretima | i) European earthworm
(b) Lumbrix
(ii) South Indian earthworm
(c) Neanthus
(iii) Earthworm
(d) Megacolex
(iv) Sandworm
questions.explanation: Option A is the right choice since anchor the earthworm names first: Pheretima (spelt Ferretima here) is the common Indian earthworm—pair (a) with (iii). Lumbricus is the European earthworm—(b)–(i). Nereis is the marine polychaete 'sandworm'—(c)–(iv). Megascolex is the large South Indian earthworm—(d)–(ii). That grid is a–iii, b–i, c–iv, d–ii—option A. Swapping Nereis with Lumbricus breaks marine vs terrestrial ecology. You can eliminate B (ii i iii iv), C (iv ii i iii), D (iii ii i iv) — each one conflicts with the principle or calculation that leads to option A. questions.text:
Consider the following statements about phylum Arthropoda and select
the correct option.
(a) Animals of the phylum Arthropoda are the only invertebrates that fly in the air.
(b) Animals in this phylum have simple or compound eyes.
(c) Animals in this phylum have lungs for respiration.

options.D: All of the above are correct.

questions.explanation: Among invertebrates only arthropods (chiefly class Insecta) achieve powered flight—(a) is a classic exam line. Compound and simple eyes both appear across Chelicerata and Mandibulata—(b) holds. Respiration spans tracheae in insects, book lungs in arachnids, and gills in many crustaceans; 'lungs' in (c) is syllabus shorthand for book lungs/tracheal air breathing. All three statements are accepted here.

questions.text:
Consider the following statements about the Phylum Echynodermata and
choose the correct statement option.
(a) These are triploblastic, unisexual, radial symmetric animal.
(b) These animals do not have the ability to regenerate.
(c) These animals obtain food mainly from such aquatic circulatory systems.

options.D: All of the above are correct

questions.explanation: Echinoderms are triploblastic, coelomate, and usually dioecious with radial (pentamerous) symmetry—(a) passes. They are famous regenerators—starfish arms, sea-cucumber evisceration—so (b) is outright wrong. The water-vascular system drives tube feet for locomotion and food gathering from the substrate/water column—(c) is the functional truth. Keep (a) and (c).

questions.text:
Consider the following statements about the superclass Pisces and choose
the correct option.
(a) It is a class of fishes.
(b) The heart of these animals is composed of three chambers and has a single
circulatory system.
(c) They are warm blooded animals.
(d) These animals are oviparous and external fertilization occurs.
questions.explanation: Option C is correct because Pisces is the superclass/class of true fishes—(a) is definitional. Most bony and cartilaginous fishes are oviparous with external fertilisation in water—(d) matches standard reproduction notes. Fish hearts are typically two-chambered (one auricle, one ventricle), not three—(b) is incorrect. All fishes are poikilothermic (cold-blooded)—(c) is incorrect. Only (a) and (d) remain. You can eliminate A (Only (a), (b), (c) are correct), B (Only (b), (c), (d) are correct), D (Only (a), (b), (d) are correct) — each one conflicts with the principle or calculation that leads to option C. If the question asks what is incorrect, identify the false statement first and then match it to the answer choice.

questions.text:
Consider the following statement about phylum Tenofera and select the
correct option.
(a) Animals in this phylum are called sea-walnuts, sea-gooseberries.
(b) Pleurobrachcia is also known as comb jelly.
questions.explanation: The answer is option C: Phylum Ctenophora (Tenofera in the paper) holds sea walnuts and sea gooseberries—translucent comb-plate swimmers—so (a) is correct. Pleurobrachia is the textbook comb jelly—(b) is correct. Treat both as one phylum's common names and examples. Distractors A (Only (a) is correct), B (Only (b) is correct), D (Both (a) and (b) are incorrect) look plausible but do not follow from the facts stated in the question. Store the reasoning behind the answer, not just the letter, because topic packs revisit the same idea in different forms.

questions.text:
Consider the following statements about class-Aves and choose the
correct option.
(a) It has the highest body temperature among all vertebrates.
(b) Birds have no sense of smell but their eyes are sharp.
(c) They have preen glands on their skin which maintain the feathers.

options.D: All of the above are correct

questions.explanation: Birds (Aves) maintain the highest body temperature among vertebrates thanks to endothermy and insulation—(a) is syllabus canon. Vision dominates; many birds have reduced olfaction (though not absolutely 'no smell')—(b) is accepted in this set. Preen (uropygial) glands secrete oil for feather maintenance—(c) is standard. All three lines stand together.

questions.text:
Non-chordates have which of the following characteristics?
(a) The body does not have a support called notochord.
(b) The pharynx does not have larynxes.
(c) If there is a nerve chord, it is paired, solid and on the ventral side of the
body.

options.D: All of the above are correct

questions.explanation: Non-chordates lack a notochord/vertebral column—(a) is the defining negative trait. Gill slits in the pharyngeal wall and a dorsal hollow nerve cord are chordate hallmarks; non-chordates lack the pharyngeal gill-pouch plan described in (b). Where a nerve cord exists in lower invertebrates it is ventral, solid, and often paired—(c) captures that contrast. All three bullets describe non-chordate diagnostics in this paper.

questions.text:
Consider the following statements and choose the correct statement
option.
(a) Nidaria animals use tentacles to inject poison into the prey.
(b) Cnidoblasts are used by animals of the order Nidaria to capture prey.
questions.explanation: Option D is the right choice since Cnidarians immobilise prey with nematocysts discharged from cnidocytes/cnidoblasts—tentacles are the delivery site, but the statement 'inject poison through tentacles' without naming cnidoblasts is marked wrong here. 'Order Nidaria' is a misspelling; the valid taxon is Cnidaria/Coelenterata. Both (a) and (b) is wrong as written—choose the 'both incorrect' option. Distractors A (Only (a) is correct), B (Only (b) is correct), C (Both (a) and (b) are correct) look plausible but do not follow from the facts stated in the question. MPSC papers often recycle this type of detail, so read the question carefully before you commit to an option.

questions.text:
Match the correct pairs.
Phylum
Example
(a) Porifera | i) Hydra, Physelia
(b) Cilantrata | ii) Tapeworm, Liver fluke
(c) Platyhelminthes | iii) Sycon, Spongilla
(d) Nemathelminthis | iv) Ascaris, Wucheria
questions.explanation: Porifera examples are Sycon and Spongilla—sponge genera—so (a) maps to (iii). Hydra and Physalia belong to Cnidaria—(b) to (i). Tapeworm and liver fluke are flatworms (Platyhelminthes)—(c) to (ii). Ascaris and Wuchereria are roundworms (Nemathelminthes)—(d) to (iv). Grid b–iii, a–i, c–ii, d–iv is option B.

questions.text:
Consider the following statements about the phylum Porifera and choose
the correct option.
(a) Animals in this group excrete ammonia.
(b) They contain blood circulation and nervous system.
(c) These animals have the ability of regeneration.

options.D: All of the above are correct

questions.explanation: Option C works here because Sponges excrete nitrogenous waste largely as ammonia by diffusion across cell membranes—(a) is fine. They lack true blood vessels and a centralised nervous system—(b) is false. Fragmentation and high regenerative capacity are Porifera trademarks—(c) is true. Ammonia excretion plus regeneration gives (a) and (c). You can eliminate A (Only (a), (b) are correct), B (Only (b), (c) are correct), D (All of the above are correct) — each one conflicts with the principle or calculation that leads to option C. questions.text:
Consider the following statements about Phylum Nidaria and choose the
not incorrect option.
(a) Animals of this group reproduce by budding method.
(b) Animals of this group have nervous system in primitive stage.
(c) The anatomy of these animals is polyp and medusa.

options.D: All of the above are correct

questions.explanation: Option D is correct because Hydra and many cnidarians reproduce asexually by budding—(a). A nerve net (diffuse nervous system) is the primitive cnidarian plan—(b). Polyp and medusa are the two body forms—(c). All three are standard Coelenterata/Cnidaria notes in Maharashtra zoology texts. Distractors A (Only (a), (b) orrect and (c) incorrect), B (Only (b), (c) correct and (a) incorrect), C (Only (a), (c) correct and (b) incorrect) look plausible but do not follow from the facts stated in the question. Keep the name, formula, and unit together in your notes — that helps you spot incomplete distractors quickly.

questions.text:
Consider the following statements about Platyhelminthes and select the
correct option.
(a) The bodies of these animals are double -layered and bilaterally symmetrical.
(b) These animals use suckers to stick to the host and hooks to absorb nutrients.
questions.explanation: Flatworms are acoelomate triploblastic bilaterians—'double-layered' in (a) misstates their organisation (they have mesoderm). They attach with suckers and feed through a muscular pharynx; hooks on scolex absorb nothing—nutrients cross the tegument—so (b) scrambles attachment vs absorption. Both statements are incorrect.

questions.text:
Match the correct pairs.
(a) Turbellaria | i) Tapeworm
(b) Trematoda | ii) Planaria
(c) Cestoda | iii) Liver fluke
questions.explanation: Option B matches the question because Turbellaria = free-living flatworms like Planaria—class (a) pairs with (ii). Trematoda = flukes including liver fluke—(b) with (iii). Cestoda = tapeworms—(c) with (i). Sequence ii–iii–i is option B. Putting tapeworm under Turbellaria is the common trap. You can eliminate A (i ii iii), C (i iii ii), D (iii i ii) — each one conflicts with the principle or calculation that leads to option B. MPSC papers often recycle this type of detail, so read the question carefully before you commit to an option.

questions.text:
Observe the following statements.
(a) In Aschehelminthes the number of cells is same from birth to death is
called Eutely.
(b) Most of these animals cause disease in humans.
questions.explanation: Choose option C: Eutely means a fixed cell number from birth to death in some nematodes—(a) is textbook Aschelminthes trivia. Ascaris, Wuchereria, hookworm, and pinworm are major human parasites—(b) is broadly true. Both statements together form the correct answer. Distractors A (Only (a) is correct), B (Only (b) is correct), D (Both (a) and (b) are incorrect) look plausible but do not follow from the facts stated in the question. If the question asks what is incorrect, identify the false statement first and then match it to the answer choice.

questions.text:
Study the following statements about phylum Annelida.
(a) Animals of this group are triple layered , rod-shaped, bilaterally symmetrical.
(b) These animals do not have Setae for propagation.
(c) These animals can be brackish water, freshwater as well as amphibians.

options.A: All of the above are correct

questions.explanation: Annelids are triploblastic, coelomate, bilaterally symmetrical segmented worms—(a). Setae/chaeetae aid grip and locomotion in earthworms and polychaetes—so (b) 'no setae' is false. They inhabit marine, freshwater, moist terrestrial, and even brackish niches—(c). Triploblastic segmentation plus habitat breadth gives (a) and (c).

questions.text:
........... these animals are known as indicators of water pollution as they
thrive in mud.
questions.explanation: The correct answer is option B — Tubifex worms colonise oxygen-poor, organic-rich mud and sewage—making them classic bio-indicators of organic pollution. Lumbricus, Pheretima, and Megascolex are cleaner-soil earthworms, not pollution-thriving mud specialists. You can eliminate A (Lumbrix), C (Megacolex), D (Ferretima) — each one conflicts with the principle or calculation that leads to option B. Keep the name, formula, and unit together in your notes — that helps you spot incomplete distractors quickly.

questions.text:
Consider the following statements about Arthropoda and choose the
correct option.
(a) The body of these animals is three layered, bilaterally symmetrical.
(b) These animals have jointed feet for movement.
(c) The body of these animals is segmented and is divided into three parts
namely head, thorax and abdomen.

options.D: All of the above are correct

questions.explanation: Arthropods are triploblastic coelomates with bilateral symmetry—(a). Jointed appendages define the name Arthropoda—(b). Tagmatisation into head, thorax, and abdomen (or cephalothorax + abdomen) is the body plan in insects and many allies—(c). All three are core phylum characters here.

questions.text:
Consider the following statements about Suborder Mandibulata.
(a) The body of an animal in the class Insecta is divided into head, thorax and
abdomen.
(b) Animals of this class do not have pigment in their blood.
(c) Animals of the class- Kilopoda are herbivorous and non-venomous
arthropods.
Identify the correct statement/s from the above

options.D: All of the above are correct

questions.explanation: Insecta bodies show head–thorax–abdomen division—(a). Insect blood (haemolymph) lacks respiratory pigments like haemoglobin—(b). Class Chilopoda (centipedes/'Kilopoda') are carnivorous and venomous through forcipules—(c) as 'herbivorous and non-venomous' is false. Only (a) and (b) pass.

questions.text:
Match the correct pairs.
(a) Asterodi | i) Mouth facing front
(b) Aphiurody
(ii) Movement through the medulla
(c) Crinidae
(iii) Digest food outside the body
(d) Ekaynodi
(iv) No arms, filaments
(e)
Holourody
v) The mouth is backward
questions.explanation: The answer is option A: asteroidea (starfish) everting the cardiac stomach to digest prey outside the body matches (a)–(iii). Ophiuroidea (brittle stars) have the mouth on the oral surface facing forward—(b)–(i). Crinoidea (sea lilies) are mouth-upward suspension feeders—(c)–(v). Echinoidea move via the water-vascular/ambulacral system—(d)–(ii). Holothuroidea (sea cucumbers) lack arms, using tentacle-like buccal filaments—(e)–(iv). Option A is the consistent map. You can eliminate B ((a)-(ii), (b)-(i), (c)-(iii), (d)-(iv),…), C ((a)-(iii), (b)-(i), (c)-(v), (d)-(iv), …), D ((a)-(iii), (b)-(i), (c)-(iv), (d)-(v), …) — each one conflicts with the principle or calculation that leads to option A. If the question asks what is incorrect, identify the false statement first and then match it to the answer choice.

questions.text:
Consider the following statements about Phylum Cordata and select the
correct option.
(a) All animals have a notochord which transforms into the skull and spinal cord.
(b) No gills or lungs for respiration.
(c) On the lateral side there is a nerve chord which transforms into a nervous
system.

options.D: All of the above are correct

questions.explanation: Option C matches the question because Chordates possess a notochord (often replaced by vertebral column), a dorsal hollow nerve cord, and pharyngeal gill slits at some life stage—(a) and (c) align with syllabus summaries even if wording is loose. 'No gills or lungs' in (b) is false—larval gills or adult lungs/tracheae appear across the phylum. Pair (a) with (c). Distractors A ((a) and (b) correct), B ((b) and (c) correct), D (All of the above are correct) look plausible but do not follow from the facts stated in the question. Store the reasoning behind the answer, not just the letter, because topic packs revisit the same idea in different forms.

questions.text:
Choose the correct classification of Aves from the given options below.
Kingdom
Phylum
Sub-phylum
questions.explanation: Birds are vertebrate chordates: Kingdom Animalia, Phylum Chordata, Subphylum Vertebrata (Vertebrata). Cephalochordata (Amphioxus) and Urochordata (tunicates) are non-avian subphyla; Hirudinea is leeches in Annelida—a deliberate distractor.

questions.text:
Match the correct pairs.
(a) Exocites | i) Sucker fishes
(b) Hippocampus | ii) Flying fish
(c) Remora | iii) Dog fish
(d) Scolydan | iv) Sea horse
questions.explanation: Exocoetus is the flying fish—(a)–(ii). Hippocampus is the sea horse—(b)–(iv). Remora attaches with a dorsal sucker disc—(c)–(i). Dogfish (Scoliodon/Squalus) is a cartilaginous shark—(d)–(iii). Option C (ii–iv–i–iii) is the only internally consistent set.

questions.text:
Consider the following statements about Sub-phylum Reptilian and choose
the correct option.
(a) These animals are cold blooded and mostly terrestrial.
(b) Legs are very short or absent in these animals.
(c) These animals are unisexual ,oviparous and fertilization takes place within
the body.
(d) Animals do respiration by gills.

options.D: All of the above are correct

questions.explanation: The correct answer is option A — Reptiles are poikilothermic and predominantly terrestrial—(a). Limblessness or reduced limbs (snakes, some lizards) is common—(b). Internal fertilisation with shelled eggs (oviparity) typifies the class—(c). Adult reptiles breathe by lungs, not gills—(d) is false. (a), (b), and (c) stand. Distractors B (Only (a), (c), (d) are correct), C (Only (b), (c), (d) are correct), D (All of the above are correct) look plausible but do not follow from the facts stated in the question. questions.text: ............. called glass snake.
questions.explanation: Ophisaurus is the glass lizard/'glass snake'—a legless anguid lizard, not a true snake. Hydrophis is a sea snake; Natrix and Typhlops are other serpent genera.

questions.text:
Observe the following statements.
(a) The study of lizards is called saurology.
(b) The study of fishes is called ecthyology.
questions.explanation: Option C is correct because Saurology is the study of lizards—(a). Ichthyology (paper spells 'ecthyology') is the study of fishes—(b). Both etymology-based terms are accepted as correct in this key. questions.text:
Observe the following statements and choose the correct statement
option.
(a) Animals of the order Porifera have collar cells.
(b) Nidaria/Cilentrata animals have tentacles.
questions.explanation: The answer is option C: Choanocytes (collar cells) with flagella line sponge canals and drive water current—characteristic Porifera cells—statement (a). Cnidarians bear tentacles armed with cnidocytes—statement (b). Both phylum markers are true. Distractors A (Only (a) is correct), B (Only (b) is correct), D (Both (a) and (b) are incorrect) look plausible but do not follow from the facts stated in the question. questions.text: The body organization of unicellular animals is ...........
questions.explanation: Unicellular animals (Protozoa) show protoplasmic grade of organisation—life processes occur at the single-cell level without tissues. Higher grades (cell–tissue, tissue–organ, organ system) need multicellularity.

questions.text:

(b) Body symmetry
(c) Herbivores-Carnivore

Organs of Locamotion

questions.text:

questions.text:
Choose the correct statements.
(a) Colony living - Corals, Sea-Anemone
(b) Solitary living - Hydra, Jellyfish
questions.explanation: Option C works here because Colonial cnidarians include corals and sea anemones—(a). Solitary forms include Hydra and many jellyfish medusae—(b). questions.text: .............. is known as “Portuguese man of war”.
questions.explanation: The Portuguese man-of-war is the colonial siphonophore Physalia (sometimes linked with Obelia in older regional notes as a floating colonial cnidarian). Aurelia is a true jelly; Chironex is box jelly; corals are anthozoans—not the correct name here.

questions.text:
Consider the following statement/s about Aschehelminthes.
(a) The body of these animals is tri-layered and bilateral-symmetrical.
(b) These animals are endoparasitic and unisexual.
(c) They are called roundworms or True worms.

options.D: All of the above are correct

questions.explanation: Roundworms (Nematoda/Aschelminthes) are triploblastic pseudocoelomates with bilateral symmetry—(a). Most exam parasites (Ascaris, hookworm, filarial worm) are dioecious—(b). They are called roundworms/nematodes—(c). All three statements are bundled as correct.

questions.text:
